Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice N.S.Sanjay Gowda
 Oral Judgment

(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice N.S.Sanjay Gowda)
1.

The claimant is in appeal challenging the exoneration of the liability on the insurer and also is also seeking for enhancement.
2.
The Tribunal has recorded a finding that an accident did occur and the same was due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the motorcycle.
It has, however, proceeded to exonerate the liability of the insurer on the ground that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess a driving licence.
Learned counsel for the insurer, places reliance on the judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & Others.

entities.text: Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is to be stated here that the said judgment can have no application to the present facts of the case, and the judgment can only be relatable to the special facts of that particular case.
In fact, in Para 8 of the order, the Supreme Court has categorically observed as "in the facts of the present case", the order was being passed.

4. The other judgment upon which reliance is placed, i.e., Civil Appeal Nos.7220-7221 of 2011 in the case of Bali Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another would also not be of any avail because, in that Mohammed Khan vs Tukaram And Anr on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108542875/
2 particular case the Supreme Court was dealing with a situation where, the owner had employed a driver and the Supreme Court had found that the owner had not even taken reasonable care to see whether his driver had got his licence renewed.

entities.text: Bali Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mohammed Khan vs Tukaram And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The context of that case was regarding the employment of a NC: 2024:KHC-K:6919 driver for driving a truck, which was ostensibly for a commercial purpose and therefore, a responsibility was cast on the owner to ensure that the driver that he had employed was a competent person.
Obviously, the situation of present case is completely different and can have no application.

5. In the light of the judgment of the full court in Yallavva's case, in such cases where, it is contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a driving licence, the only remedy available to the insurer would be to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
Consequently, to this extent, the order is modified.
6. The Tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.4,000/- and assessed the disability at 6%.
So, in my view, in the light of the evidence adduced, the assessment of disability at 6% cannot be found fault with.

However, since there was no proof of income, the amount of NC:
2024:KHC-K:6919 Rs.7,000/- fixed by KSLSA for accidents of the year 2013 will have to be adopted.
7. Since the claimant was aged 35 years, a multiplier of '16' has to be applied.

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.80,640/- (Rs.7,000x12x16x6%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8.
In respect of the other heads of compensation, it is noticed that the same are adequate and does not require any enhancement.

9. Consequently, the claimant, in modification of the impugned award are entitled for the following sums:
